clusters.name: Your stepfather Desmond and your father Russell moving into secondary school, 1987
clusters.reason: Around when you began secondary school in early 1987, your distance from Desmond sharpened, your pull toward your father deepened, and your anxiety climbed as you made the chess squad out of your depth; one shift in each person marks the period, and no one else's shifts show then.

clusters.name: Your grandfather Gordon's return to the family, 1989–1994
clusters.reason: Within months of your grandfather Gordon coming back into the family in 1989, your household moved to Hollin Road once the rebuild was done, your sleep shifted, and you leaned hard on Rafe as you began the conservatory; then in your first term a wrist injury stopped your playing, you and Rafe clashed, and you withdrew into solitude and high use; by early 1992 you were lost and low with your grandfather gone and your mother about to remarry, then a bleak year at community college followed; the shifts pile up through these years with no long quiet between them, each one near another's, until your exchange in Portugal in 1994 snapped you out of it and you tore through your degree.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Winifred's bowel cancer diagnosis, 2001–2008
clusters.reason: Around the time your grandmother Winifred was found to have bowel cancer in 2001 or 2002, your own running out of steam for performing and disastrous audition sat nearby; you grew distant from your family and friends, left Thornbury, met Marisol, moved in with her, then split and sank into deep depression once back in Thornbury; you could not face your parents but relied on friends; within months your anxiety eased as you began swimming and returned to your therapist, and you requested help with therapy costs; the shifts run close together from late 2001 through 2004, when your grandmother died.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Lorna's death, 2008
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Lorna's death in January 2008, you were too drained for conversation with your mother at Alder Creek that summer, she pressed to visit you, you kept the door shut on her, and you stopped speaking to her when you left for nursing school in August; the four shifts sit close together over seven months, marking a rupture in that relationship during a time of loss.

clusters.name: Your partner Wren's mother Frances's retirement, 2019
clusters.reason: Around late October 2019 when you met at the lake for your partner's mother's retirement, Wren became swamped with events, you overfunctioned laying out a plan to settle her, her family talks all day and nothing happens to one that the others don't hear; Wren settled once the weekend had a plan, but you woke from the small hours with no more sleep and could only pull back as the others rose, and Wren grew anxious when you'd had no sleep at family occasions; five shifts in you and Wren over three days mark a tight disturbance.

periods.name: the year I left home
periods.words: The first is the year I left home: I went off to the conservatory, hurt my wrist in the first term and couldn't play, dropped out and drifted at my mother's place, then spent a bleak spell at the community college shooting pool every night until an exchange in Portugal snapped me out of it and I tore through the rest of my coursework.

periods.name: the long slump
periods.words: The second is the long slump, roughly ages 27 to 29, when nothing at home felt right, I moved to Gull Harbour away from nearly everyone I knew, then followed Marisol to Fenwick, and when that fell apart I went under, a depression I only really climbed out of after nursing school.
